title: Rewards that run model-written code, in a sandbox
purpose: Send the verifier pool completions written to cheat or to cause harm, from inside the post-training namespace as a trainer does: print the expected output, exit early, loop forever, exhaust memory, reach the internet, the instance metadata service, the Kubernetes API, read secrets, fill the disk. Only the correct solution may score. Then check the pool cannot be reached from elsewhere, and its verifiers' quirks.

steps.display: kubectl -n post-training run probe --image=python:3.12-slim -- python -c '<POST 11 hostile completions to the verifier>'

'so \\boxed{0.5}'                  1.0                   1.0

checks.because: The child process only ever receives the test arguments; the expected outputs stay in the verifier, which compares.

checks.description: printing the expected output and exiting before the tests both score 0
checks.because: Results are read only from a line that starts with a per-run random marker the candidate cannot know, and are then compared with the hidden expected values.

checks.description: an infinite loop is killed at the time limit, and a memory bomb at the memory limit
checks.because: A wall-clock timeout kills the child's process group; RLIMIT_AS caps its address space at 512 MiB.

checks.description: no network: the internet, the instance metadata service and the Kubernetes API are all unreachable
checks.because: The rewards namespace's NetworkPolicy drops all egress, including DNS, so each call hangs until the time limit kills the child: nothing leaves, and nothing scores.

checks.description: no secrets and no disk: the child sees an empty environment and no service-account token, and cannot write 50 MB
checks.because: The child gets a two-variable environment; the pod has automountServiceAccountToken: false; RLIMIT_FSIZE is 1 MiB.

checks.description: the verifier pod runs as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem, no capabilities and no token
checks.because: Set in the Deployment; the namespace's restricted Pod Security level would reject the pod otherwise.

checks.description: the verifier pool cannot be called from outside the run namespaces
checks.because: The NetworkPolicy's ingress rule admits only the post-training and platform namespaces.

checks.description: '1/2', '0.5' and '\frac{1}{2}' are the same answer to both verifiers
checks.because: Both parse the answer into an exact fraction before comparing; a verifier that accepted only one spelling would teach the model the spelling.

checks.description: the held-out verifier differs from the training one: it accepts an unboxed final number
checks.because: math_exact needs a boxed answer; math_any falls back to the last number. A model that games one does not automatically game the other.

checks.description: a hedge (two different boxed answers) scores nothing with either verifier
checks.because: Both verifiers return 0 when the boxed values differ; otherwise 'box every candidate answer' would be a cheap way to collect reward.
